items.title: John Lamb interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 16, 2001
items.q: And he taught me out of the Simandl Book, Franz Simandl.

ctx.x: Yeah, and had a little tuba experience because I had done that before. So I was a little bit ahead of the game. But I said I have to really do something about my abilities. I says, I decided right there and then that I was going to become the world’s greatest bass player. I decided, that’s what I put into my head. I says you have to do it. I don’t know why, I think I was sort of like driven and I had experienced hunger, and I experienced the disappointments and all those kind of things. And I had a craving or a…

you know what I mean? Anyway, I went back in the Air Force and I did this thing, and within six months I had an awakening. I mean really. I hit a low one day and then I had to go through these changes. I don’t know, it’s mental, physical, and it’s like an awareness came over me. I began to investigate spirituality a little bit. Psychology. All the books that I could read on the subjects that were on the base library I began to investigate. And I got rid of all my jazz records. And I had a whole slew of, I just…
